question: In what time (in years) will ₹2,500 fetch an interest of ₹1,000 at 10% per year simple interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 1 year = 10% of **₹2,500** = **₹250**

Total interest to be fetched = **₹1,000**

**Time** = Total Interest ÷ Interest per year

⇒ **Time** = 1000 ÷ 250 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,500

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹1,000

**Rate (R)** = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c145dd59f81b4564a611278147ec8ec41980e034b373221e61e1a4926789b1d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1000 = (2500 × 10 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1000 = 250 × T

⇒ T = 1000 ÷ 250

⇒ T = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

Amount (A) is the sum of Principal (P) and Interest (I). Formula: A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100 or A = P(1 + RT/100).

Compound Interest (CI) vs Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas CI is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes to double your money: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate (usually applied to Compound Interest).
